title: Rubato overview
description: issue → node → session → cost, and the signals that must never be silent. Metric names from crates/rubato-protocol/src/otel.rs.

panels.title: Trust check: is the signal flowing?
Launches by outcome
panels.description: Launch results per companion (ADR 0070): started, refused (by rubato_reason, for example missing_dependency when tmux is missing or below the pin) and failed (a git or tmux call that failed or hit its deadline; the error is in LaunchResult.error and on the queue entry as "did not start: …"). A rise in failed after an upgrade is the git worktree path breaking where tmux-ide used to work: look for the rubato.launch log line with launch_id and outcome.

panels.title: MCP calls by tool and outcome
panels.description: The companion's MCP server for launched sessions (ADR 0071): calls by rubato_mcp_tool, rubato_outcome and rubato_reason (refused no_launch: a launch the companion does not know, often after a restart that lost launches.json; identity: a call naming another issue; discovery: Claude Code asking for OAuth after a 401, a stale token in mcp.json). Reports drained (sent, or not_sent server_too_old while the server does not take agent_mcp). Not initialized: a launched session made no MCP request in its first five minutes, so Claude Code could not start the server; look for the rubato.mcp.call span and the 'launched session has not initialized mcp' log line with rubato.launch_id.

panels.title: Sessions by state
panels.description: Sessions of every companion by state, from each companion's latest snapshot (rubato.sessions.by_state, recorded by the server only, #43). A companion whose socket ended counts its sessions that had not ended as unknown, and one silent for RUBATO_COMPANION_SILENT_SECS with its socket open (a laptop asleep) does too, until it says Hello or sends again (#69). A revoked companion counts 0. Unknown is never working: compare with Companions (heartbeat). The log line companion disconnected says what was recorded (sessions=unknown, zeros or left_to_newer); companion quiet, sessions counted unknown marks a silent one.

panels.title: Blocked, by station left from
panels.description: Blocked issues by the rail station they left from (ADR 0043); the sum equals the blocked bar of Issues by state. off_rail equal to that count means blocked_from is not being set. B: blocking hooks by cause; no idle_prompt while building rises means every block reads mid-turn.

panels.title: Map age
panels.description: Seconds since the loaded map was loaded. Healthy: a saw-tooth up to the reload cycle (about 6-7 min at the default poll interval). It grows without bound when reloads stop or keep failing; the cause is on the Map panel (load failures).

panels.title: Cost is a signal (Claude Code OTel, rubato.* resource attributes)
Spend history writes
panels.description: Writes of each issue's spend history (ADR 0037), by outcome: stored (a session's spend changed and the issue's point was written), unchanged (same or older value), rejected (not finite or negative), failed (the write errored; log 'companion bookkeeping write failed' with write=record_spend). A flat stored line while working sessions is above zero means companions stopped sending spend (no pricing configured?) or the write fails.

panels.title: Backlog age
panels.description: Seconds since each repo's open issues were last listed. Healthy: under the poll interval. It grows when the listing fails (token or installation access, rate limit, GitHub down); the Issues tab then says 'could not list'. A repo the map no longer names reports 0 and is left out.

panels.title: Backlog issues
panels.description: Open issues listed per repo. Flat at 500 means the listing is cut and the Issues tab says 'first 500 shown'.

panels.title: Web writes rejected
panels.description: Web requests refused by a rule, by route and reason: unknown_id, kind_mismatch, unknown_repo (an issue of a repo no map names, on pins, launch and queue), not_on_team, team_record_stale, installation_lookup_failed, token_exchange_failed and user_lookup_failed (login, log line 'login failed' with step), session_expired, companion_taken (on /api/pair/approve: a code for a companion paired to another person, #160), field_too_long and pending_cap (on /api/pair/start: a hostname or version over 255 characters, or too many codes waiting for approval, #168; logged as user anonymous), cross_origin (a write or websocket from another origin, ADR 0066; warn line 'cross-origin request refused' with origin and sec_fetch_site; behind a proxy, check RUBATO_PUBLIC_URL is the origin the browser sees)., and on the settings routes (/api/settings, /api/workspaces, /api/w/{ws}; ADR 0075): bad_id, duplicate, same_map, default_kept, id_has_rows, map_source_fixed, map_file, draft_open, map_invalid, repo_unreadable (the member's own GitHub token cannot read the map repo or a repo the map names, or Rubato holds no token for them), url_refused, no_token_key, dev_traffic_set, changed_meanwhile (a stale edit), open_login and bad_value. Each has an info log line 'web write rejected' with the user.

panels.title: Repos not covered
panels.description: Repos the map or a tracked issue names that the GitHub App installation does not cover. Their branches, plans and pull requests cannot be read; each is a finding on the map and a warn line 'repo not covered by the installation' with rubato.repo. Fix: add the repo to the App's installation.

panels.title: Layout writes
panels.description: Accepted writes to the shared map layout, by arrangement: flat is the map (ADR 0016), grouped the By repo grouping (ADR 0068). A part or box dragged to a new place, or an arrangement cleared with Auto-arrange (info lines 'layout written' and 'layout cleared' with rubato.user and rubato.layout.arrangement). A flat count that moves while people only use By repo means a grouped move reached the flat map. If people see different maps and this moves, the write landed: look at 'Web clients' and at 'Events dropped' with reason web_lagged. If it does not move, look at 'Web writes rejected' for /api/layout.

panels.title: Queue depth
panels.description: Issues queued per companion (what its owner intends to run there), recorded every poll tick for every pairing, 0 for an empty or revoked one. Queues that grow while 'Sessions by state' stays flat are intent without sessions: a question for the person, not a fault. A start that did not start keeps its entry and logs 'queue entry kept, launch not started' with rubato.companion_id and rubato.issue.

panels.title: Map proposals
panels.description: Map proposals by how they ended: opened, failed (a GitHub step refused or timed out), withdrawn, merged, closed. A failure has an error log line 'map proposal failed' with the step (head, file, ref, contents, pull, close), repo, branch, base sha and rubato.user: check the GitHub App's Contents and Pull requests permissions and that it is installed on the map repo. Propose again resumes; Withdraw gives up. The draft's size is rubato_map_draft_ops.

panels.title: Map proposal age
panels.description: How long the map proposal has been in its current state. While it is opening or merged the draft is frozen and nobody can edit the map, so past 15 minutes those two turn yellow. Stuck opening: read the 'map proposal failed' log line, then Withdraw. Stuck merged: the map has not been loaded since the merge, check 'Map age' and 'Poll ticks'. Proposed may be old: a review takes time. Each transition logs 'map proposal state' with from, to, the pull request and the base sha. Empty when there is no proposal.

panels.title: Map lines
panels.description: Map: lines read from the open-issues listing (ADR 0026), by outcome: pinned (a member's line placed its issue), already_pinned, unknown_id and kind_mismatch (the line names no part or seam of that kind in the map; the issue stays in Not pinned), unknown_repo (the issue's repo is not named by that workspace's map), counted once per line; untrusted_author (someone outside the team wrote the line, so it is only a suggestion), counted per listing. Each tick logs 'backlog placement' with listed, map_lines, untrusted, suggested and none. Lines stop being read if the listing fails: see Backlog age.

panels.title: Issues created
panels.description: Issues created from Rubato's 'New issue here…' (ADR 0025), by outcome: created (GitHub answered), found (GitHub did not answer, and the listing found the issue by its Rubato-Request line), failed (refused with a 403, or unseen for ten minutes), ignored (a Rubato-Request line on an issue the App did not write, per listing; logs 'request line ignored' with the author and reason, issue #165). 'opening' is how many creations wait for a confirmation now. A failure logs 'issue creation failed' with step (create, unseen), rubato.repo and request_id: a 403 means the installation lacks Issues: write (an admin approves it; Rubato reads the permission every full poll pass). Refusals before sending are in 'Web writes rejected' under route /api/issues.

panels.title: Approvals
panels.description: Issues whose newest approval names an earlier version of the plan (finding 'ApprovalStale', ADR 0027): the plan changed after a team member commented 'Approved: plan <sha>'. Ticking task checkboxes does not count as a change. The overview names each issue with both shas; ask its owner to re-approve or revert. Reviews and approvals are read from comments by OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR authors on the full poll lane (every 300 s); one that is ignored logs 'approval ignored' or 'review ignored' with the reason (a Bot, or the author's association). Decision: comments follow the same rule (ADR 0065) and log 'decision ignored'. Not 0 for longer than a review takes is a question for a person, not a fault.

panels.title: Findings by workspace
panels.description: What the map and the plans disagree about, per workspace (issue #89, ADR 0045): plan ids no map of the issue's workspaces has, plans that fit none of them, ids that name two different parts across workspaces sharing a repo, and approvals of an earlier plan version. An issue two workspaces hold counts in each, so read one workspace at a time; never sum across them. Each line names its workspace; the overview of that workspace (?w=<id>) lists the issues.

panels.title: GitHub calls by endpoint
panels.description: GitHub REST calls per minute, one per page (ADR 0032). The budget is 5000 per hour.

panels.title: Traffic report age
panels.description: Seconds since the latest good traffic report was observed (ADR 0039). The first question at 3 am: is it fresh? Past 3 × the source's fetch interval (default 180 s) the overview says stale and the Traffic lens draws unknown; alert TrafficReportStale fires past 600 s. One value per workspace with a traffic source (ADR 0075). No value for a workspace means it has no source set in Configure workspace (and RUBATO_DEV_TRAFFIC is unset), which is not a fault. If it climbs, look for the log lines 'traffic source failing' and 'traffic report rejected' (with rubato.reason) and the span rubato.traffic.fetch.

panels.title: Quiet seams and undeclared edges
panels.description: Map versus territory (AGENTS.md): declared seams with no calls while both parts show traffic (finding SeamQuiet), calls between parts no seam joins (UndeclaredTraffic), ghost parts: services that emit a namespace but no part names (ObservedOnlyPart, ADR 0059), discrepancies a person dismissed for the workspace (ADR 0060), and unidentified ends: no namespace and no part declaring that name. Only meaningful while the report is fresh: a stale or failing source yields 0 of each. Ghosts above 0 with nothing lit usually means the parts do not declare `service` yet; unidentified ends above 0 mean a caller's peer.service names something no part declares. Dismissals are logged with who: 'traffic dismissal added' / 'removed'. One series per workspace (ADR 0075).

panels.title: Traffic fetches
panels.description: Traffic report fetches per hour by outcome: ok, rejected (outside the limits: too_many_edges, bad_window, name_too_long, parse; the previous report is kept) and failed (the source did not answer; the state turns failing). One fetch per workspace every fetch interval of its source. Split by workspace (ADR 0075) and by rubato_traffic_source (prometheus or dev_file, ADR 0040). A source whose stored secrets no longer open is failing with secrets_unsealable. For prometheus, failed means the query API did not answer, answered non-2xx or status error; the log line traffic source failing carries which.

panels.title: Skills emitting
panels.description: Calls from skills and plan-check to other parts per hour, from the OTel servicegraph connector metrics the traffic source reads (ADR 0040, 0061). Each rubato.skill.call span with peer.service makes one edge: rubato → github, plan-file, system-map. A launched session (rubato.launch) whose skill draws nothing here means the RUBATO_OTEL_* mirror did not reach the session (seam companion-claude-code): check the launch script exports and that the developer environment has an OTLP endpoint and service.namespace. Empty everywhere: no endpoint is configured, or the connector does not run.

panels.title: Session messages by outcome
panels.description: Messages people sent from Rubato to their own launched sessions, as they settle (ADR 0051): delivered, not_idle (the session was working; queued again), refused (the reason is in the log line), failed, interrupted and delivery_unknown (pushed, no answer while the companion stayed live, never pushed again). A rise in delivery_unknown is a companion that receives but does not answer: look for 'session message delivery unknown' with rubato.session_message.id, and the companion's rubato.session_input.deliver span.

panels.title: Oldest message waiting for an idle session
panels.description: Seconds the oldest queued message has waited while its launched session waits for input (last hook Stop or idle_prompt). It should drain within a dispatch; a climbing line is a queue that does not move: the companion is not live, lacks session_input, or keeps answering not_idle. Alert SessionMessageStuck (plan 122 PR 7).

panels.title: Companions by capability
panels.description: Connected companions per capability they announced in Hello (ADR 0051). Planning in Rubato is switched on (the cutover) only once every companion shows session_input; one that does not is an older companion its owner must upgrade.

panels.title: Approvals waiting for handoff
panels.description: Approvals in Rubato delivered to their session more than 30 minutes ago, still current, with no matching commit on the branch and no committed handoff report (ADR 0055). Above 0 for 30 minutes pages ApprovalNoHandoff. Look at the session's log for the rubato.plan.handoff line: plan_changed or bundle_changed means ask for a new approval; push_failed means a rerun pushes the same commit.

panels.title: Link comments missing
panels.description: Handoff commits on a branch whose link comment is not on the issue yet (ADR 0055): the approver's token is missing (finding LinkWaitingForApprover) or a post's outcome is unknown (LinkCommentWaiting). Above 0 for 30 minutes pages HandoffNoLinkComment; the rubato.plan.link_comment span says which.

panels.title: Approval records that differ
panels.description: Plans read at the branch head whose approved_by, approved_at or approved_sha differ from Rubato's approval, or that carry keys Rubato never wrote (finding ApprovalRecordMismatch, ADR 0054). No link comment is posted for them. Above 0 for 5 minutes fires ApprovalRecordMismatch.

panels.title: Draft revisions
panels.description: Draft revisions stored from launched sessions' settle points, and bundles refused by reason (too_large, no_plan, owner_conflict, unknown_launch; ADR 0053). Revisions at zero while sessions plan means the companion's mirror stopped or lacks the drafts capability.

panels.title: Session log
panels.description: Prompts and replies stored in the session log from hook payloads (ADR 0052), and entries dropped by reason. Entries at zero while sessions work means hooks stopped carrying the text.

panels.title: Headless turns
panels.description: Headless companions (agent-only clients, ADR 0062): turns ended per minute by outcome (ok, failed, no_result, timeout, killed) and turns the companion killed by reason (stop, cap, revoke, timeout, quiet, companion_restarted). A kill by timeout, quiet or companion_restarted fires HeadlessTurnsKilled; no_result rising means turns end without a stream-json result.

panels.title: Plan status pushes
panels.description: PlanStatus pushes to companions for their launched sessions (ADR 0071): welcome (right after a companion connects, from the last tick) and change (a tick found a different status), by outcome: sent, offline (the companion's socket was gone), no_summary (the launch's issue is in no built overview). With companions connected and launched sessions live, welcome flat at zero means plan_status answers unknown everywhere: look for 'plan status pushed after welcome' and 'overview not built' with rubato.workspace.

panels.title: Webhooks
panels.description: GitHub App webhook deliveries by outcome (ADR 0074), seconds since the last accepted one, the oldest unapplied one, and changes the catch-up poll found that no delivery brought. Absent while RUBATO_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset. Healthy: accepted deliveries whenever the team works, catch-up changes at zero, pending under 60 s.

targets.legendFormat: seconds since the last accepted delivery

panels.title: Voice
panels.description: A plan room's voice channel (ADR 0073), absent while RUBATO_VOICE is off. Speech calls per minute by op (stt, tts) and outcome (ok, timeout, status, transport, bad_body, empty, busy); the p95 seconds of each op; join tokens minted; failed joins the browser reported by reason (signal, ice, permission, insecure, other). SpeechProviderFailing fires when every call failed for 10 minutes. Joins failing as ice mean UDP or TURN; as insecure, Rubato is not on HTTPS.

panels.title: Workspace config changes
panels.description: Every stored change to a workspace's settings (ADR 0075): the info line 'workspace config changed' with rubato.workspace, rubato.user and keys, the names of what changed (name, map_ref, traffic.url, traffic.secrets.headers, default_spend_cap_usd, created, deleted). Never a value. The same change is the span rubato.workspace.config_changed. A refused change is not here: see Web writes rejected.

panels.title: Fleet requests by action and outcome
panels.description: A person's own lead agent and its workers (ADR 0072), absent while RUBATO_ORCHESTRATOR is off. Fleet requests per minute by action (list, launch, message, stop), outcome and reason, and fleet notices queued and coalesced. other_owner or identity fires FleetCrossOwner: a lead named another person's session or a lead it does not own. not_led is the owner's own session the lead did not start; fleet_full and someone_elses_issue are a lead asking for too much.

panels.title: Every part on the Traffic lens (ADR 0082, ADR 0083)
Web spans relayed
panels.description: Posts to the web's span relay (POST /api/telemetry/traces, ADR 0082) per hour by outcome: forwarded (rewritten and sent to the OTLP endpoint), off (the server exports no traces; the web stops), unauthenticated, too_large, invalid, rate_limited (past the per-login bucket), export_failed (the OTLP endpoint refused or did not answer; the log line telemetry relay export failed carries the status). Dropped spans are those the rewrite would not vouch for: an unknown route, not client-kind, or out of time. Forwarded with no web-server pipe on the Traffic lens: see HTTP trace context.

panels.title: HTTP trace context
panels.description: HTTP requests per hour by what their traceparent gave (ADR 0082): linked (a server span under the web's client span: the web-server pipe), absent (assets, health checks, scripts) and invalid. Linked falling while the web is used, or invalid rising, means the web's calls stopped pairing with the server's on the service graph.

panels.title: Traffic lookback
panels.description: Traffic lookbacks per hour by outcome (ADR 0083): ok, failed, timeout. The lookback asks the service graph over 6 h, 1 d and 7 d on the first fetch and every tenth, after the window's report. A failing one keeps the previous answer, or claims nothing: quiet parts then read without a last seen, never as not seen. The log line traffic lookback carries rubato.traffic.seen.
